analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: Nasdaq futures cooled from +1.11% to +0.7% while the S&P held +0.7% and the Dow firmed to +0.5% — the holiday bounce is intact but no longer accelerating. The genuinely new items since 6 AM are the S&P CreditWatch Negative on Nvidia (multi-outlet confirmed, and Moody's holding Aa1 stable is the offset), the reported Nvidia server-shipment freeze to four Southeast Asian nations, the ECB minutes landing hawkish (a large number of members could have backed an October hike; Dec 17 now looks like a near-done deal), Apple closing out November as the Mag7 winner (+3.3%) with Nvidia the worst, Anthropic clawing back to just under its $83 IPO price, and oil pushing higher again on Houthi strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports. Signal vs noise: the CreditWatch plus the shipment freeze are signal — they keep the governance and export-control overhang on Nvidia alive even after Huang's return and the stock's +18.9% week; the ECB's hawkish tilt is priced (EUR/USD unmoved near 1.0975); Wednesday's Nasdaq 100 reversal (-4.7% intraday to -0.6% close, seen only 16 times since 1988) is the context that makes Friday's follow-through question real. Any single futures tick on a closed Thanksgiving morning is noise, and Friday's thin half session can amplify the first move either way. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines, so community_signals is empty.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US index futures hold their gains on Thanksgiving morning: Dow +0.5%, S&P 500 +0.7%, Nasdaq-100 +0.7% (IBD, ~09:17 ET), with the Nasdaq cooling from +1.11% at 06:06 ET; the rebound went global — European semis rallying, SK Hynix, Delta Electronics and Hon Hai among the biggest EM gainers, Kioxia and SoftBank up double digits in Tokyo.
headlines.why_it_matters: The dip-buying momentum is holding into the holiday pause and spreading globally — but overnight futures on a closed market do not guarantee Friday's open.

headlines.headline: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA credit rating on CreditWatch Negative on Wednesday, warning of a possible one-notch downgrade to AA- within 90 days unless governance concerns are addressed; Moody's kept its Aa1 rating with a stable outlook.
headlines.why_it_matters: Huang's return did not settle the governance question — S&P cites board independence, succession planning and key-man risk, so the overhang persists even after the stock's 18.9% weekly gain.

headlines.headline: Nvidia reportedly froze server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, per reports circulating Thursday morning.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. If true, it revives the export-control risk S&P explicitly flagged, and it hits the same Southeast Asia channel investors watch for China-adjacent demand.

headlines.headline: ECB minutes show a large number of policymakers could have backed a rate hike at the October meeting; the account says another hike would likely be necessary unless the inflation outlook improves significantly, reinforcing a 25bp hike at the Dec 17 meeting (deposit rate 2.50%, euro-area inflation 4.0% in October).
headlines.why_it_matters: Another central bank leaning hawkish alongside the Fed's near-certain December hike — but EUR/USD was virtually unchanged near 1.0975, so the December move is already priced.

headlines.headline: Apple is on track to be November's Magnificent Seven winner, up 3.3% for the month for a fifth straight monthly gain, with a market cap now nearly $2 trillion above Microsoft's; Nvidia is the month's worst Mag7 performer, third at a $3.6 trillion market cap.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rotation within Big Tech is the month's story — Apple's steadiness vs Nvidia's governance-driven whipsaw shows the AI trade is splitting into winners and questioned names, not moving as one block.

headlines.headline: Oil pushes higher again after Yemen's Houthis struck Saudi Red Sea ports; US crude futures rose about 1% Thursday after WTI closed Wednesday at $83.68 (+2%). Copper jumped more than 3% off an 11-month low.
headlines.why_it_matters: Supply-threat premium is building in energy and metals alongside the equity rebound — a second front to watch into the OPEC+ meeting this weekend.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) reversed off a record low of $73.85 to close Wednesday at $82.79 (+1.1%), hovering just under its $83 IPO price after pricing at $83 and opening at $111.50 last week.
headlines.why_it_matters: The IPO name that helped trigger the AI-trade wobble is stabilizing near its issue price — a small tell that the post-IPO air pocket may be closing.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news overnight. New today: a Seeking Alpha note (Nov 26) rates USAC a Hold — 8.88% yield covered, but limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt — countering yesterday's buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield, 1.67x distribution coverage and record pricing. Carry-forward: Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24), FY2027 at $1.31; Q3 2026 (Nov 3): revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6; $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
